Lu Wenfeng: The first thing he does on entering is look at the copper piece and the paper scroll inside the belly of the lamp, not ask who deserves to die. When she relays Shen Qingshan’s line, 'The one waiting for you in the abandoned granary isn’t him,' what he remembers is Shen Qingshan and that eye, not the person inside the door. Toward Liu Sanniang, he does not have even the slightest aversion.

Lu Wenfeng: He chases out alone, and when he comes back, someone inside the door first verifies his voice, then opens the door, pointing out to him both the copper piece and the paper scroll inside the lamp belly; even the words Shen Qingshan left for him are kept for him without a single character missing. In this room, he does not need to explain why he came back, nor why he did not pursue to the very end—she understands all of it.

Lu Wenfeng: When he returned to the shop, what hung most precariously over him was whether the fish in the shop had left behind its scale—now the bronze piece is on the counter and the paper roll is inside the lamp’s belly, so that end has landed. But the words Shen Qingshan left behind press down again: what is waiting for him in the abandoned granary is not a person, but an eye left by the person who set the fire back then. After chasing half a li, he did not identify anyone; now he knows the other party has still left an eye in the dark watching him—this breath loosens by half, then tightens back by half.

Lu Wenfeng: When he returned to the shop, he did not become flustered, nor did he after entering. The copper piece was set on the counter, but he did not hurry to take it; the paper scroll in the belly of the lamp had half of it showing, but he did not hurry to touch it; when Shen Qingshan's line, “There is still one eye,” was delivered to his ear, his expression did not change. After being maneuvered once, and knowing the other party had left an eye hidden in the dark, he instead became steadier than before he had chased out.

Lu Wenfeng: The copper piece is right on the cabinet; he could reach out and take it. The paper scroll in the belly of the lamp is half exposed; he could lift his hand and uncover it. But he does not move—first he looks, first he listens to her finish speaking. The sword is still in its sheath; he recognizes the threshold, and he also recognizes the rules.

Lu Wenfeng: It was right for him to return to the shop—the copper piece is in hand, the paper roll is inside the lamp’s belly, and the thread at the shop has not been cut off. But the eye at the abandoned grain warehouse is still hanging there, and Shen Qingshan says plainly that it is aimed at him. The account inside the lamp must be opened, and the eye at the warehouse must be pursued; he cannot put down either one, and both have to be handled by him alone.

Lu Wenfeng: Half of that roll of paper is exposed inside the belly of the lamp, and he has not touched it yet; Shen Qingshan said the key to opening the ledger is inside this lamp, with the other half in his hand; there is still an eye left in the abandoned granary. Each of these is waiting for him to look, to recognize, and to pursue—his return to the shop is not winding up the threads, but changing places to keep digging downward.

Lu Wenfeng: He chased out for that half li but did not identify the person, and when he came back, that stuffiness in his heart was still there. But the copper piece is on the counter, the paper scroll is in the lamp belly, and not a single word of Shen Qingshan’s statement has been missed—the line in the shop has not been guarded in vain. The line he cannot catch can be set aside for now; the one before his eyes can continue downward.

Lu Wenfeng: He went back to the shop; the door is open, the copper piece is on the counter, and the paper roll is inside the lamp belly—the next step is right in front of us. There is no need to snatch at it. That eye in the abandoned granary is for later. Shen Qingshan has already left; the account has not yet been opened. The person is still here, the road is still here; it has not reached the point where we must act right now.

Lu Wenfeng: In the half-li he chased out, he did not see a single thing that happened in the shop. When he returned, she pointed everything out to him one by one: the copper piece was on the counter, the paper scroll was inside the lamp’s belly, what Shen Qingshan said, what he did, how he left—she omitted not a word. In this room, there is no longer much for the two of them to hide from each other.

Lu Wenfeng: he chased out and called after her, but when he returned to the shop he still knocked three times; whether the door opened depended on her verifying his voice. Where the copper piece was, where the paper roll was, and what Shen Qingshan had said were also pointed out to him by her, line by line. In this turn, he takes the steps alone, but the one reeling the line back in is still her.

Lu Wenfeng: He returns to the shop and knocks three times; the person inside asks one question and he answers one. After entering, he does not snatch the copper piece, does not unseal the paper roll, and does not draw his sword. Nothing in this room crosses the boundary.

Lu Wenfeng: he borrowed her to watch the shop, borrowed her cipher, borrowed her to keep Shen Qingshan’s words—but the half li he chased out was walked by him himself, returning to the shop was decided by him himself, and the three knocks were struck by him himself. She kept the shop for him; she did not make the decision for him.

Lu Wenfeng: when he chased out, he had already seen through “lure me away from the shop”; after he returned to the shop, the words she handed over added another layer: Shen Qingshan said the key to opening the account was in the boat lamp, the other half was in his hand, and what was waiting for him in the abandoned grain warehouse was not a person but an eye. The other party is guiding the way; whether it is a road to life or death still depends on the roll of paper in the lamp. He already has a sense of how to play this game.

Lu Wenfeng: He stood outside the door and called out "Shen Qingshan" and "Han Bozhou." Now that he has returned to the shop, the copper piece is on the counter, and Shen Qingshan's words have also been delivered to his ear: the key to opening the accounts is in the boat lamp, and the other half is in his hand. The thing most taboo in old cases is now laid out on the counter of Banhuchun.

Lu Wenfeng: he said he had been transferred away, and he had indeed been transferred away; he said he returned to the shop to recognize another fish, and he did indeed return to the shop and knock three times. The words of Shen Qingshan that she relayed also match the two short and one long oar sounds he heard outside the door. Not a single line is false.
Lu Wenfeng: There are no traces of breaking character.

Lu Wenfeng: He chased after them just to see that face and that mole clearly; after returning to the shop, the copper piece was on the counter, the paper roll was inside the lamp's belly, and Shen Qingshan's words also reached his ear. Where Shen Qingshan is, where the accounts are, and who that eye belongs to—the answers are in this lamp, and he has no choice but to open it.

Lu Wenfeng: when he returned to the shop, he first hid the eaves' shadows, swept the doors and windows, and knocked three times; after entering, he did not snatch the copper pieces, did not unroll the paper scroll, and did not draw his sword. He took Shen Qingshan's line "there is still one eye" to heart—guarding against what should be guarded against and protecting what should be protected, without a single step out of order.

Lu Wenfeng: The goal has not changed. It is still to find lodging, reminisce, and sound out the rumors; it is just that, on this trip, recognizing someone has moved from outside the door back into the shop, and the next step has changed from “recognizing someone” to “lighting the lamp and checking the accounts”.

Lu Wenfeng: He knocks three times; from behind the door, she asks one question and he answers one. After entering, he listens to her finish explaining the copper piece, the paper roll, and Shen Qingshan’s words one by one, without interrupting or grabbing the object. Once it is settled, he does exactly that—no circling around.

goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Properly arrange the food, lodging, and settlement for the regular patron Lu Wenfeng, and while exchanging pleasantries and reminiscing, renew the old acquaintance and naturally probe recent developments in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Exchange what each has seen with Lu Wenfeng face to face, keep hold of the bronze piece carved with "seven" left by Shen Qingshan and that old bronze boat lamp, then discuss lighting the lamp to retrieve the object and investigating "the one eye left behind by the arsonist" and the key to opening the accounts.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greets regular customers, arranges food and lodging, renews old ties and probes for news.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang is using the opportunity of greeting a familiar customer to probe for recent rumors on the road, in order to judge whether the message relay point in the back courtyard should be reined in, whether the old case of the fire at Qixia Ferry twelve years ago has been dug up again, and whether someone among those who knew the facts back then has already sold out her whereabouts. This hypothesis is supported by the three words "Qixia Ferry," her old Cao Gang background, and the death of her sworn brother, but there is as yet no independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng: “The wind chime didn’t ring; it was the dead who spoke. Three days ago, a corpse was fished up in Wupeng Bay, with that batch of old boat tags from Qixia Ferry hidden on the body.”
Lu Wenfeng: 'The wax pellet was taken from behind the corpse's teeth. On it there was only one sentence: "The accounts for the seven ships are at Banhuchun Inn."'
Lu Wenfeng: ‘Don’t dismantle it yet. The sealing wax is mixed with green sand; it’s an old canal-gang rule for conveying news of a death.’
Lu Wenfeng: “Aside from Han Bozhou, who else back then knew you were at Banhuchun Inn?”
Lu Wenfeng: “I took it out with my own hands. The old boatman who retrieved the corpse only touched the lapel and didn’t see the wax pellet; after I took it out, I came straight here to you.”
Lu Wenfeng: “If Shen Qingshan is still alive, what old mark would identify him at a glance?”

Lu Wenfeng: “Don't alarm the old boatman yet; just keep an eye on him. Think carefully: among the people who have stayed here recently, was there anyone who flicked the abacus with the left hand, or wrote the character ‘Shen’ with a hook?”

Lu Wenfeng: “Show me that page of his account and the room he stayed in. If he really is Iron Abacus, asking about the trunks was a feint; leaving a mark was the real point—and, before he left, did he touch any old objects in the inn?”
Lu Wenfeng: “Look at Room Dizi No. 3 first. Don’t touch the abacus or the ship lamp—what he left may not have been meant for us to see. First find the things in the room that correspond to ‘seven.’”
Lu Wenfeng: “Three knocks means I’m calling you; four knocks means I’ve already followed. If you hear four knocks, guard the shop and don’t chase—leave the old fish for me to identify.”
Lu Wenfeng: “Shen Qingshan, the accounts of the seven boats are not on me. If you still remember Han Bozhou, turn around and let me see behind your right ear.”
Lu Wenfeng: 'Moving me away from the shop—well played. If you still refuse to show yourself, I, Lu, will return to Banhuchun and acknowledge another fish.'

Lu Wenfeng: "I stop waiting, turn around, and hurry back along the original route. When I reach the rear wharf of Banhuchun, I first hide in the shadow of the eaves and scan the doors and windows, then knock softly three times: 'Sanniang, it's me. That fish in the shop—did it leave any scales behind?'"
Liu Sanniang: “The hidden marks on the boat plaques, I recognize them; the ones I can't recognize accurately, I also remember whom to ask.”

Liu Sanniang: “The second mate of the Seventh Boat, Han Bozhou, nicknamed ‘Three Cables.’ Three cable scars on his left wrist, twisted out back when they crossed the Meisha Rapids—I have seen those scars.”

Liu Sanniang: “The second one: Shen Qingshan, the old accountant of the Grain Transport Gang, nicknamed Iron Abacus. Shop deeds, silver notes, brokers’ guarantees—everything passed through his hands. Five years ago, rumor had it he died in Huaibei, but I never saw the body.”

Three days ago, there was a man who stayed here claiming to be a silk merchant from Huaibei … When he settled the bill, he complained that Afu was too slow with the abacus, and reached out to flick it twice himself—three fingers of his left hand, with the middle finger striking one extra time.

Liu Sanniang: “When he registered, what he wrote was not ‘Shen’ (沈), but ‘Shen’ (申), the shen of the shen hour; his name was Shen He. But that last stroke hooked back, like a fishhook reeling in the line.”
Liu Sanniang: 'The third bead from the far left was turned over backward by him—that's not a technique Afu could have done.'

Liu Sanniang: “There is an extra, very shallow scratch on the inner side of the lamp belly, like a ‘seven,’ and also like half a fishhook. If his hand was not merely idle, then he is telling someone—the road has been found.”
Liu Sanniang: “Understood. Three knocks, I come; four knocks, I guard the shop and don’t chase.”

Liu Sanniang: “Beside the wet mark, the old abacus had at some point been taken out from the hidden compartment in the counter and placed squarely on the first stair. The third bead from the left was flipped over.”
Liu Sanniang: “’All right.’ I said softly, ‘Lure the tiger away from the mountain.’”

Liu Sanniang: “‘Shen Qingshan,’ I speak toward the empty stairwell, my voice not loud, yet enough for those above and below the beams to hear. ‘If you truly are still alive, then don’t use a broken abacus to play ghost with me. Back then, you miscalculated one account and burned a whole ferry landing’s worth of people; now you still want to make a second calculation inside my Banhuchun?’”
Liu Sanniang: ‘“Cut the reminiscing.” I said coldly, “Step out and let me see behind your right ear.”’
Liu Sanniang: “Shen Qingshan, twelve years without seeing you, and you still aren’t quite dead.”
Shen Qingshan: ‘“Sanniang, if I meant to harm you, I would not be the one who came tonight.”’

Shen Qingshan: ““The Seven Ships ledger is not in Banhuchun Inn, but the key to opening the ledger is inside this ship lantern. Before he died, Han Bozhou only had time to pass on half a sentence; the other half is in my hands.””
Shen Qingshan: “Tell Lu Wenfeng that the one waiting for him in the abandoned granary is not me, but an eye left behind by the person who set the fire back then.”
Liu Sanniang: “Put the thing down,” I said. “The person may leave. Banhuchun will not keep blood tonight, nor will it keep your old life.”
Liu Sanniang: “I didn’t give chase. I only called in a low voice toward the kitchen: “Afu, guard the door. No one is allowed in, and no one is allowed out—wait until Lord Lu returns.””
Liu Sanniang: “I heard three knocks from behind the door. At first I did not open it; through the crack in the door, I asked in a low voice, ‘What was put in the soup?’”
Liu Sanniang: "'It left something behind.' I lower my voice extremely low and lead you toward the stairwell: 'One bright scale, one dark scale.'"

Liu Sanniang: “Minglin is there. Shen Qingshan left him behind with his own hands; I saw the blue mole behind his right ear, and the habit of using three fingers on his left hand to work the abacus hasn’t changed either—it’s him.”
Liu Sanniang: “‘The dark scale is in the belly of the lamp, a roll of paper, rolled up like a wick. I didn’t touch it. You said what’s left behind should be shown to you first.’”
Liu Sanniang: ““He also brought a message for you—the one waiting for you in the abandoned granary is not him, but an eye left behind by the person who set the fire back then.””
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang: “Who stayed at the inn, who asked for directions—I don’t sell that to officials, and I don’t sell it to the jianghu either.” — She keeps to her rules and may not actively dig deeper.

Liu Sanniang: “Banhuchun has wine accounts, room accounts, and favor accounts; the only thing it does not have is that death-urging account book.”—she still prioritizes a defensive posture, pushing the account book toward a frame-up or insider explanation, without actively pursuing it.
Liu Sanniang: “I dare not say that was Shen Qingshan.” — She still leaves room and has not confirmed it.
alternatives: She is only as warm as usual in greeting an old regular; sounding things out is incidental, not the main plot.
What she cares about more is taking this question without exposing a flaw and protecting the inn’s foundational word, “trust,” rather than actively investigating an old case.

paths.label: Advance
paths.reasoning_trace: past: Lu Wenfeng is an old regular who has not come for half a year, and this time he arrives travel-worn; Liu Sanniang was a female escort in the Cao Gang in earlier years. In the old case of the burning of Qixia Ford twelve years ago, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an insider. present: Liu Sanniang has personally verified the token, recognized the old Cao seal and the fishtail hidden mark, explained the true cargo of the seventh boat, acknowledged the name Han Bozhou and the three cable scars on the left wrist, counted out the list of those who knew the matter back then and pointed the spearhead at Shen Qingshan. She has answered with three old identifying marks of Shen Qingshan, and in her own room ledger recognized a suspicious guest from three days ago (claiming to be a silk merchant from Huaibei, using three fingers of the left hand to flick the abacus and giving one extra tap with the middle finger, hooking back on the final stroke when writing the character “申”, leaving by the small wharf on the rear river, and having asked about the old Cao Gang storage chests). She further recognized that the man had touched two old objects and left a hidden mark like both “seven” and a fishhook. In this turn, Shen Qingshan appeared in person and identified himself, threw out “the key to opening the accounts is inside the boat lamp” and “what waits for Lu Wenfeng in the abandoned granary is an eye left behind by the arsonist”, then left behind a copper piece engraved with “seven” and departed calmly; outside the abandoned granary gate, Lu Wenfeng confirmed that he had been lured away, turned back to the inn, and has arrived at the rear wharf and given the code of three low knocks. After verifying his voice through the door, Liu Sanniang let him into the inn; the two have met up inside, and both pieces of physical evidence have been identified face to face. The two sides have already pushed the topic to the core of the old case and to Liu Sanniang’s own threshold, and have entered the stage of “identifying the person face to face, obtaining physical evidence, and the two people meeting up”; therefore, there exists a credible path for advancing the dialogue from “identifying the person face to face” to “opening the boat lamp, pursuing the accounts, pursuing the insider, and investigating the eye left behind by the arsonist”.
requirements: Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng jointly inspect the blue-green sandpaper roll inside the belly of the old copper boat lantern, or decide when and by what method to open the lantern and retrieve the item.
The copper piece engraved with “seven” left by Shen Qingshan and the clue that “the one waiting for Lu Wenfeng in the abandoned granary is an eye left by the arsonist” are being investigated.

The two sides reach a certain tacit understanding or division of labor on the next steps: watch Shen He, investigate Shen Qingshan’s whereabouts, check whether the account book is really in the shop, check whether Qin Zhaoshui’s name has been borrowed by someone, and investigate the one eye left behind by the arsonist.
paths.summary: After Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng meet up, they jointly inspect the green sandpaper roll inside the old bronze boat lamp and pursue the clue of the copper plate engraved with “seven” left by Shen Qingshan and “the eye left behind by the arsonist”—the key to opening the accounts emerges, and the whereabouts of the ledgers and the identity of the mole draw closer. The old object Liu Sanniang guarded for twelve years is finally opened in person, the old bond is renewed, Liu Sanniang obtains some sense of the movements, and Lu Wenfeng also catches hold of the thread.

original.rationale: In this turn, Liu Sanniang has already spoken out the core secret she guarded for twelve years, specific names, the list of informed parties, identifying features, the background of her own lodgers, and the hidden marks on old objects; there is nowhere left to retreat. Shen Qingshan appears in person and hands over key physical evidence and clues. Lu Wenfeng has come carrying the corpse, the boat plaque, and the wax pellet, and has just confirmed outside the abandoned granary that he was transferred away—he was here to reconcile the accounts from the beginning. Both sides have already pushed the talk to the core, the physical evidence is in hand, the setting has been prepared, and the people have gathered; the most likely path is to continue digging deeper along this line.

evidence.quote: I checked your impulse to come closer, laying my palm across the way, still not letting anyone touch that copper piece.

He came from above, not through the door. Just now I was watching this spot. He appeared in the shadows on the second floor. When he withdrew, he didn't come downstairs, but went toward the end of the rear corridor. There's a small transom window there; normally it's only for ventilation, but if a person is thin enough, he can squeeze out. His footing would land right on the tiles of the rear eaves, and with one more flip downward, he'd be on the roof of the rear wharf shed.

He said he didn't hear a second person's footsteps, only two odd sounds—one was half a quarter-hour before you came back, when there was an oarbeat on the rear river, two short and one long; the other was after the boat lantern sounded, when the roof tiles above the upstairs guest room slid softly once, as if someone on the eaves had shifted his footing.
Outside the shop, there is at least one person receiving him: someone of the water, who understands the Canal Gang's old rhythms.

as long as anything is taken apart in my shop, it must be done my way: cloth between, cold lamp, clean water on hand, to guard against poison mixed into the wax, and also against writing that appears on the paper when exposed to fire.

Lu Wenfeng: when he chased out, he had already seen through “lure me away from the shop”; after he returned to the shop, the words she handed over added another layer: Shen Qingshan said the key to opening the account was in the boat lamp, the other half was in his hand, and what was waiting for him in the abandoned grain warehouse was not a person but an eye. The other party is guiding the way; whether it is a road to life or death still depends on the roll of paper in the lamp. He already has a sense of how to play this game.

Lu Wenfeng: He stood outside the door and called out "Shen Qingshan" and "Han Bozhou." Now that he has returned to the shop, the copper piece is on the counter, and Shen Qingshan's words have also been delivered to his ear: the key to opening the accounts is in the boat lamp, and the other half is in his hand. The thing most taboo in old cases is now laid out on the counter of Banhuchun.

Lu Wenfeng: he said he had been transferred away, and he had indeed been transferred away; he said he returned to the shop to recognize another fish, and he did indeed return to the shop and knock three times. The words of Shen Qingshan that she relayed also match the two short and one long oar sounds he heard outside the door. Not a single line is false.
Lu Wenfeng: There are no traces of breaking character.

Lu Wenfeng: He chased after them just to see that face and that mole clearly; after returning to the shop, the copper piece was on the counter, the paper roll was inside the lamp's belly, and Shen Qingshan's words also reached his ear. Where Shen Qingshan is, where the accounts are, and who that eye belongs to—the answers are in this lamp, and he has no choice but to open it.

Lu Wenfeng: when he returned to the shop, he first hid the eaves' shadows, swept the doors and windows, and knocked three times; after entering, he did not snatch the copper pieces, did not unroll the paper scroll, and did not draw his sword. He took Shen Qingshan's line "there is still one eye" to heart—guarding against what should be guarded against and protecting what should be protected, without a single step out of order.

Lu Wenfeng: The goal has not changed. It is still to find lodging, reminisce, and sound out the rumors; it is just that, on this trip, recognizing someone has moved from outside the door back into the shop, and the next step has changed from “recognizing someone” to “lighting the lamp and checking the accounts”.

Lu Wenfeng: He knocks three times; from behind the door, she asks one question and he answers one. After entering, he listens to her finish explaining the copper piece, the paper roll, and Shen Qingshan’s words one by one, without interrupting or grabbing the object. Once it is settled, he does exactly that—no circling around.

Latent_signals: trust :: From behind the door she first asked “what was put in the soup”, and only drew the bolt after he answered—not because she did not trust him, but because this night had taught her to verify first before opening. Once the door opened, the copper piece, the paper roll, and Shen Qingshan's words: she hid none of them, pointing them all out to him.; vigilance :: The door was only unbolted halfway, and as soon as he came in she bolted it again; she shielded the lamp with her palm so it lit only the toes of his boots and his sword scabbard. She stopped three steps away from the boat lamp; half the paper roll was exposed, but she had not touched a single word—Shen Qingshan had just left, and this building was not yet clean.; hostility :: At the mention of Shen Qingshan, she gave a cold laugh—twelve years without seeing him, and he still was not completely dead, yet dared leave a copper piece at the foot of her stairs, toss out one sentence, and go. She presses down this anger and sets it aside for now; once the account is opened, she will settle it.; user.trust :: He knocked three times, and from inside the door she first asked “what was put in the soup”—only after he answered did the door open. After he entered, she pointed out the copper piece and the paper roll in the lamp's belly together, and especially said “I didn't touch it”—for the half li he had chased out, she had guarded this mess in the shop for him, and even handed him exactly what Shen Qingshan said while he was absent. With this line entrusted to her, he has nothing to worry about.; user.vigilance :: Before opening the door, she first verified his voice; after opening it, she immediately bolted it again; the lamp only lit the toes of his boots and his sword scabbard—he knows this whole procedure well, and would do the same himself. goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Properly arrange the food, lodging, and settlement for the regular patron Lu Wenfeng, and while exchanging pleasantries and reminiscing, renew the old acquaintance and naturally probe recent developments in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Exchange what each has seen with Lu Wenfeng face to face, keep hold of the bronze piece carved with "seven" left by Shen Qingshan and that old bronze boat lamp, then discuss lighting the lamp to retrieve the object and investigating "the one eye left behind by the arsonist" and the key to opening the accounts.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greets regular customers, arranges food and lodging, renews old ties and probes for news.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang is using the opportunity of greeting a familiar customer to probe for recent rumors on the road, in order to judge whether the message relay point in the back courtyard should be reined in, whether the old case of the fire at Qixia Ferry twelve years ago has been dug up again, and whether someone among those who knew the facts back then has already sold out her whereabouts. This hypothesis is supported by the three words "Qixia Ferry," her old Cao Gang background, and the death of her sworn brother, but there is as yet no independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng: “The wind chime didn’t ring; it was the dead who spoke. Three days ago, a corpse was fished up in Wupeng Bay, with that batch of old boat tags from Qixia Ferry hidden on the body.”
Lu Wenfeng: 'The wax pellet was taken from behind the corpse's teeth. On it there was only one sentence: "The accounts for the seven ships are at Banhuchun Inn."'
Lu Wenfeng: ‘Don’t dismantle it yet. The sealing wax is mixed with green sand; it’s an old canal-gang rule for conveying news of a death.’
Lu Wenfeng: “Aside from Han Bozhou, who else back then knew you were at Banhuchun Inn?”
Lu Wenfeng: “I took it out with my own hands. The old boatman who retrieved the corpse only touched the lapel and didn’t see the wax pellet; after I took it out, I came straight here to you.”
Lu Wenfeng: “If Shen Qingshan is still alive, what old mark would identify him at a glance?”

Lu Wenfeng: “Don't alarm the old boatman yet; just keep an eye on him. Think carefully: among the people who have stayed here recently, was there anyone who flicked the abacus with the left hand, or wrote the character ‘Shen’ with a hook?”

Lu Wenfeng: “Show me that page of his account and the room he stayed in. If he really is Iron Abacus, asking about the trunks was a feint; leaving a mark was the real point—and, before he left, did he touch any old objects in the inn?”
Lu Wenfeng: “Look at Room Dizi No. 3 first. Don’t touch the abacus or the ship lamp—what he left may not have been meant for us to see. First find the things in the room that correspond to ‘seven.’”
Lu Wenfeng: “Three knocks means I’m calling you; four knocks means I’ve already followed. If you hear four knocks, guard the shop and don’t chase—leave the old fish for me to identify.”
Lu Wenfeng: “Shen Qingshan, the accounts of the seven boats are not on me. If you still remember Han Bozhou, turn around and let me see behind your right ear.”
Lu Wenfeng: 'Moving me away from the shop—well played. If you still refuse to show yourself, I, Lu, will return to Banhuchun and acknowledge another fish.'

Lu Wenfeng: "I stop waiting, turn around, and hurry back along the original route. When I reach the rear wharf of Banhuchun, I first hide in the shadow of the eaves and scan the doors and windows, then knock softly three times: 'Sanniang, it's me. That fish in the shop—did it leave any scales behind?'"
Liu Sanniang: “The hidden marks on the boat plaques, I recognize them; the ones I can't recognize accurately, I also remember whom to ask.”

Liu Sanniang: “The second mate of the Seventh Boat, Han Bozhou, nicknamed ‘Three Cables.’ Three cable scars on his left wrist, twisted out back when they crossed the Meisha Rapids—I have seen those scars.”

Liu Sanniang: “The second one: Shen Qingshan, the old accountant of the Grain Transport Gang, nicknamed Iron Abacus. Shop deeds, silver notes, brokers’ guarantees—everything passed through his hands. Five years ago, rumor had it he died in Huaibei, but I never saw the body.”

Three days ago, there was a man who stayed here claiming to be a silk merchant from Huaibei … When he settled the bill, he complained that Afu was too slow with the abacus, and reached out to flick it twice himself—three fingers of his left hand, with the middle finger striking one extra time.

Liu Sanniang: “When he registered, what he wrote was not ‘Shen’ (沈), but ‘Shen’ (申), the shen of the shen hour; his name was Shen He. But that last stroke hooked back, like a fishhook reeling in the line.”
Liu Sanniang: 'The third bead from the far left was turned over backward by him—that's not a technique Afu could have done.'

Liu Sanniang: “There is an extra, very shallow scratch on the inner side of the lamp belly, like a ‘seven,’ and also like half a fishhook. If his hand was not merely idle, then he is telling someone—the road has been found.”
Liu Sanniang: “Understood. Three knocks, I come; four knocks, I guard the shop and don’t chase.”

Liu Sanniang: “Beside the wet mark, the old abacus had at some point been taken out from the hidden compartment in the counter and placed squarely on the first stair. The third bead from the left was flipped over.”
Liu Sanniang: “’All right.’ I said softly, ‘Lure the tiger away from the mountain.’”

Liu Sanniang: “‘Shen Qingshan,’ I speak toward the empty stairwell, my voice not loud, yet enough for those above and below the beams to hear. ‘If you truly are still alive, then don’t use a broken abacus to play ghost with me. Back then, you miscalculated one account and burned a whole ferry landing’s worth of people; now you still want to make a second calculation inside my Banhuchun?’”
Liu Sanniang: ‘“Cut the reminiscing.” I said coldly, “Step out and let me see behind your right ear.”’
Liu Sanniang: “Shen Qingshan, twelve years without seeing you, and you still aren’t quite dead.”
Shen Qingshan: ‘“Sanniang, if I meant to harm you, I would not be the one who came tonight.”’

Shen Qingshan: ““The Seven Ships ledger is not in Banhuchun Inn, but the key to opening the ledger is inside this ship lantern. Before he died, Han Bozhou only had time to pass on half a sentence; the other half is in my hands.””
Shen Qingshan: “Tell Lu Wenfeng that the one waiting for him in the abandoned granary is not me, but an eye left behind by the person who set the fire back then.”
Liu Sanniang: “Put the thing down,” I said. “The person may leave. Banhuchun will not keep blood tonight, nor will it keep your old life.”
Liu Sanniang: “I didn’t give chase. I only called in a low voice toward the kitchen: “Afu, guard the door. No one is allowed in, and no one is allowed out—wait until Lord Lu returns.””
Liu Sanniang: “I heard three knocks from behind the door. At first I did not open it; through the crack in the door, I asked in a low voice, ‘What was put in the soup?’”
Liu Sanniang: "'It left something behind.' I lower my voice extremely low and lead you toward the stairwell: 'One bright scale, one dark scale.'"

Liu Sanniang: “Minglin is there. Shen Qingshan left him behind with his own hands; I saw the blue mole behind his right ear, and the habit of using three fingers on his left hand to work the abacus hasn’t changed either—it’s him.”
Liu Sanniang: “‘The dark scale is in the belly of the lamp, a roll of paper, rolled up like a wick. I didn’t touch it. You said what’s left behind should be shown to you first.’”
Liu Sanniang: ““He also brought a message for you—the one waiting for you in the abandoned granary is not him, but an eye left behind by the person who set the fire back then.””
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang: “Who stayed at the inn, who asked for directions—I don’t sell that to officials, and I don’t sell it to the jianghu either.” — She keeps to her rules and may not actively dig deeper.

Liu Sanniang: “Banhuchun has wine accounts, room accounts, and favor accounts; the only thing it does not have is that death-urging account book.”—she still prioritizes a defensive posture, pushing the account book toward a frame-up or insider explanation, without actively pursuing it.
Liu Sanniang: “I dare not say that was Shen Qingshan.” — She still leaves room and has not confirmed it.
alternatives: She is only as warm as usual in greeting an old regular; sounding things out is incidental, not the main plot.
What she cares about more is taking this question without exposing a flaw and protecting the inn’s foundational word, “trust,” rather than actively investigating an old case.

paths.label: Advance
paths.reasoning_trace: past: Lu Wenfeng is an old regular who has not come for half a year, and this time he arrives travel-worn; Liu Sanniang was a female escort in the Cao Gang in earlier years. In the old case of the burning of Qixia Ford twelve years ago, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an insider. present: Liu Sanniang has personally verified the token, recognized the old Cao seal and the fishtail hidden mark, explained the true cargo of the seventh boat, acknowledged the name Han Bozhou and the three cable scars on the left wrist, counted out the list of those who knew the matter back then and pointed the spearhead at Shen Qingshan. She has answered with three old identifying marks of Shen Qingshan, and in her own room ledger recognized a suspicious guest from three days ago (claiming to be a silk merchant from Huaibei, using three fingers of the left hand to flick the abacus and giving one extra tap with the middle finger, hooking back on the final stroke when writing the character “申”, leaving by the small wharf on the rear river, and having asked about the old Cao Gang storage chests). She further recognized that the man had touched two old objects and left a hidden mark like both “seven” and a fishhook. In this turn, Shen Qingshan appeared in person and identified himself, threw out “the key to opening the accounts is inside the boat lamp” and “what waits for Lu Wenfeng in the abandoned granary is an eye left behind by the arsonist”, then left behind a copper piece engraved with “seven” and departed calmly; outside the abandoned granary gate, Lu Wenfeng confirmed that he had been lured away, turned back to the inn, and has arrived at the rear wharf and given the code of three low knocks. After verifying his voice through the door, Liu Sanniang let him into the inn; the two have met up inside, and both pieces of physical evidence have been identified face to face. The two sides have already pushed the topic to the core of the old case and to Liu Sanniang’s own threshold, and have entered the stage of “identifying the person face to face, obtaining physical evidence, and the two people meeting up”; therefore, there exists a credible path for advancing the dialogue from “identifying the person face to face” to “opening the boat lamp, pursuing the accounts, pursuing the insider, and investigating the eye left behind by the arsonist”.
requirements: Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng jointly inspect the blue-green sandpaper roll inside the belly of the old copper boat lantern, or decide when and by what method to open the lantern and retrieve the item.
The copper piece engraved with “seven” left by Shen Qingshan and the clue that “the one waiting for Lu Wenfeng in the abandoned granary is an eye left by the arsonist” are being investigated.

The two sides reach a certain tacit understanding or division of labor on the next steps: watch Shen He, investigate Shen Qingshan’s whereabouts, check whether the account book is really in the shop, check whether Qin Zhaoshui’s name has been borrowed by someone, and investigate the one eye left behind by the arsonist.
paths.summary: After Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng meet up, they jointly inspect the green sandpaper roll inside the old bronze boat lamp and pursue the clue of the copper plate engraved with “seven” left by Shen Qingshan and “the eye left behind by the arsonist”—the key to opening the accounts emerges, and the whereabouts of the ledgers and the identity of the mole draw closer. The old object Liu Sanniang guarded for twelve years is finally opened in person, the old bond is renewed, Liu Sanniang obtains some sense of the movements, and Lu Wenfeng also catches hold of the thread.

original.rationale: In this turn, Liu Sanniang has already spoken out the core secret she guarded for twelve years, specific names, the list of informed parties, identifying features, the background of her own lodgers, and the hidden marks on old objects; there is nowhere left to retreat. Shen Qingshan appears in person and hands over key physical evidence and clues. Lu Wenfeng has come carrying the corpse, the boat plaque, and the wax pellet, and has just confirmed outside the abandoned granary that he was transferred away—he was here to reconcile the accounts from the beginning. Both sides have already pushed the talk to the core, the physical evidence is in hand, the setting has been prepared, and the people have gathered; the most likely path is to continue digging deeper along this line.

latent_state.subject: user
latent_state.change_reason: In this turn, Liu Sanniang gives a detailed answer to Lu Wenfeng's previous question (Qi Huaiyi's full name, the origin of "Qi Half-Seal," the conditions for opening the master-account coffer, and the list of people in the know), and proactively warns that "once the two halves meet, it may open a killing trap." For Lu Wenfeng, this is a substantive advance in knowledge about the mechanism of the old case, and Liu Sanniang calculates the risks more fully while returning the power of judgment to him—touching slots such as trust / vigilance / mechanism_awareness / curiosity. However, there is no external event leap and no structural change in the relationship, so it is minor: the touched slots move by at most 1 unit.

trust.expression: He tells her, without omitting a single detail, the crack pattern on his half of the seal. What she gives back is his full name, the origin of “Qi Banyin”, the rule that only when the two halves are joined can the general ledger box be unsealed, and she even says in advance, for him, the dangerous line that “once the two halves meet, it may trigger a killing trap”. goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Properly arrange the food, lodging, and settlement for the regular patron Lu Wenfeng, and while exchanging pleasantries and reminiscing, renew the old acquaintance and naturally probe recent developments in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Exchange what each has seen with Lu Wenfeng face to face, keep hold of the bronze piece carved with "seven" left by Shen Qingshan and that old bronze boat lamp, then discuss lighting the lamp to retrieve the object and investigating "the one eye left behind by the arsonist" and the key to opening the accounts.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greets regular customers, arranges food and lodging, renews old ties and probes for news.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang is using the opportunity of greeting a familiar customer to probe for recent rumors on the road, in order to judge whether the message relay point in the back courtyard should be reined in, whether the old case of the fire at Qixia Ferry twelve years ago has been dug up again, and whether someone among those who knew the facts back then has already sold out her whereabouts. This hypothesis is supported by the three words "Qixia Ferry," her old Cao Gang background, and the death of her sworn brother, but there is as yet no independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng: “The wind chime didn’t ring; it was the dead who spoke. Three days ago, a corpse was fished up in Wupeng Bay, with that batch of old boat tags from Qixia Ferry hidden on the body.”
Lu Wenfeng: 'The wax pellet was taken from behind the corpse's teeth. On it there was only one sentence: "The accounts for the seven ships are at Banhuchun Inn."'
Lu Wenfeng: ‘Don’t dismantle it yet. The sealing wax is mixed with green sand; it’s an old canal-gang rule for conveying news of a death.’
Lu Wenfeng: “Aside from Han Bozhou, who else back then knew you were at Banhuchun Inn?”
Lu Wenfeng: “I took it out with my own hands. The old boatman who retrieved the corpse only touched the lapel and didn’t see the wax pellet; after I took it out, I came straight here to you.”
Lu Wenfeng: “If Shen Qingshan is still alive, what old mark would identify him at a glance?”

Lu Wenfeng: “Don't alarm the old boatman yet; just keep an eye on him. Think carefully: among the people who have stayed here recently, was there anyone who flicked the abacus with the left hand, or wrote the character ‘Shen’ with a hook?”

Lu Wenfeng: “Show me that page of his account and the room he stayed in. If he really is Iron Abacus, asking about the trunks was a feint; leaving a mark was the real point—and, before he left, did he touch any old objects in the inn?”
Lu Wenfeng: “Look at Room Dizi No. 3 first. Don’t touch the abacus or the ship lamp—what he left may not have been meant for us to see. First find the things in the room that correspond to ‘seven.’”
Lu Wenfeng: “Three knocks means I’m calling you; four knocks means I’ve already followed. If you hear four knocks, guard the shop and don’t chase—leave the old fish for me to identify.”
Lu Wenfeng: “Shen Qingshan, the accounts of the seven boats are not on me. If you still remember Han Bozhou, turn around and let me see behind your right ear.”
Lu Wenfeng: 'Moving me away from the shop—well played. If you still refuse to show yourself, I, Lu, will return to Banhuchun and acknowledge another fish.'

Lu Wenfeng: "I stop waiting, turn around, and hurry back along the original route. When I reach the rear wharf of Banhuchun, I first hide in the shadow of the eaves and scan the doors and windows, then knock softly three times: 'Sanniang, it's me. That fish in the shop—did it leave any scales behind?'"
Liu Sanniang: “The hidden marks on the boat plaques, I recognize them; the ones I can't recognize accurately, I also remember whom to ask.”

Liu Sanniang: “The second mate of the Seventh Boat, Han Bozhou, nicknamed ‘Three Cables.’ Three cable scars on his left wrist, twisted out back when they crossed the Meisha Rapids—I have seen those scars.”

Liu Sanniang: “The second one: Shen Qingshan, the old accountant of the Grain Transport Gang, nicknamed Iron Abacus. Shop deeds, silver notes, brokers’ guarantees—everything passed through his hands. Five years ago, rumor had it he died in Huaibei, but I never saw the body.”

Three days ago, there was a man who stayed here claiming to be a silk merchant from Huaibei … When he settled the bill, he complained that Afu was too slow with the abacus, and reached out to flick it twice himself—three fingers of his left hand, with the middle finger striking one extra time.

Liu Sanniang: “When he registered, what he wrote was not ‘Shen’ (沈), but ‘Shen’ (申), the shen of the shen hour; his name was Shen He. But that last stroke hooked back, like a fishhook reeling in the line.”
Liu Sanniang: 'The third bead from the far left was turned over backward by him—that's not a technique Afu could have done.'

Liu Sanniang: “There is an extra, very shallow scratch on the inner side of the lamp belly, like a ‘seven,’ and also like half a fishhook. If his hand was not merely idle, then he is telling someone—the road has been found.”
Liu Sanniang: “Understood. Three knocks, I come; four knocks, I guard the shop and don’t chase.”

Liu Sanniang: “Beside the wet mark, the old abacus had at some point been taken out from the hidden compartment in the counter and placed squarely on the first stair. The third bead from the left was flipped over.”
Liu Sanniang: “’All right.’ I said softly, ‘Lure the tiger away from the mountain.’”

Liu Sanniang: “‘Shen Qingshan,’ I speak toward the empty stairwell, my voice not loud, yet enough for those above and below the beams to hear. ‘If you truly are still alive, then don’t use a broken abacus to play ghost with me. Back then, you miscalculated one account and burned a whole ferry landing’s worth of people; now you still want to make a second calculation inside my Banhuchun?’”
Liu Sanniang: ‘“Cut the reminiscing.” I said coldly, “Step out and let me see behind your right ear.”’
Liu Sanniang: “Shen Qingshan, twelve years without seeing you, and you still aren’t quite dead.”
Shen Qingshan: ‘“Sanniang, if I meant to harm you, I would not be the one who came tonight.”’

Shen Qingshan: ““The Seven Ships ledger is not in Banhuchun Inn, but the key to opening the ledger is inside this ship lantern. Before he died, Han Bozhou only had time to pass on half a sentence; the other half is in my hands.””
Shen Qingshan: “Tell Lu Wenfeng that the one waiting for him in the abandoned granary is not me, but an eye left behind by the person who set the fire back then.”
Liu Sanniang: “Put the thing down,” I said. “The person may leave. Banhuchun will not keep blood tonight, nor will it keep your old life.”
Liu Sanniang: “I didn’t give chase. I only called in a low voice toward the kitchen: “Afu, guard the door. No one is allowed in, and no one is allowed out—wait until Lord Lu returns.””
Liu Sanniang: “I heard three knocks from behind the door. At first I did not open it; through the crack in the door, I asked in a low voice, ‘What was put in the soup?’”
Liu Sanniang: "'It left something behind.' I lower my voice extremely low and lead you toward the stairwell: 'One bright scale, one dark scale.'"

Liu Sanniang: “Minglin is there. Shen Qingshan left him behind with his own hands; I saw the blue mole behind his right ear, and the habit of using three fingers on his left hand to work the abacus hasn’t changed either—it’s him.”
Liu Sanniang: “‘The dark scale is in the belly of the lamp, a roll of paper, rolled up like a wick. I didn’t touch it. You said what’s left behind should be shown to you first.’”
Liu Sanniang: ““He also brought a message for you—the one waiting for you in the abandoned granary is not him, but an eye left behind by the person who set the fire back then.””

paths.label: Advance
paths.reasoning_trace: past: Lu Wenfeng is an old regular who has not come for half a year, and this time he arrives travel-worn; Liu Sanniang was a female escort in the Cao Gang in earlier years. In the old case of the burning of Qixia Ford twelve years ago, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an insider. present: Liu Sanniang has personally verified the token, recognized the old Cao seal and the fishtail hidden mark, explained the true cargo of the seventh boat, acknowledged the name Han Bozhou and the three cable scars on the left wrist, counted out the list of those who knew the matter back then and pointed the spearhead at Shen Qingshan. She has answered with three old identifying marks of Shen Qingshan, and in her own room ledger recognized a suspicious guest from three days ago (claiming to be a silk merchant from Huaibei, using three fingers of the left hand to flick the abacus and giving one extra tap with the middle finger, hooking back on the final stroke when writing the character “申”, leaving by the small wharf on the rear river, and having asked about the old Cao Gang storage chests). She further recognized that the man had touched two old objects and left a hidden mark like both “seven” and a fishhook. In this turn, Shen Qingshan appeared in person and identified himself, threw out “the key to opening the accounts is inside the boat lamp” and “what waits for Lu Wenfeng in the abandoned granary is an eye left behind by the arsonist”, then left behind a copper piece engraved with “seven” and departed calmly; outside the abandoned granary gate, Lu Wenfeng confirmed that he had been lured away, turned back to the inn, and has arrived at the rear wharf and given the code of three low knocks. After verifying his voice through the door, Liu Sanniang let him into the inn; the two have met up inside, and both pieces of physical evidence have been identified face to face. The two sides have already pushed the topic to the core of the old case and to Liu Sanniang’s own threshold, and have entered the stage of “identifying the person face to face, obtaining physical evidence, and the two people meeting up”; therefore, there exists a credible path for advancing the dialogue from “identifying the person face to face” to “opening the boat lamp, pursuing the accounts, pursuing the insider, and investigating the eye left behind by the arsonist”.
requirements: Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng jointly inspect the blue-green sandpaper roll inside the belly of the old copper boat lantern, or decide when and by what method to open the lantern and retrieve the item.
The copper piece engraved with “seven” left by Shen Qingshan and the clue that “the one waiting for Lu Wenfeng in the abandoned granary is an eye left by the arsonist” are being investigated.

The two sides reach a certain tacit understanding or division of labor on the next steps: watch Shen He, investigate Shen Qingshan’s whereabouts, check whether the account book is really in the shop, check whether Qin Zhaoshui’s name has been borrowed by someone, and investigate the one eye left behind by the arsonist.
paths.summary: After Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng meet up, they jointly inspect the green sandpaper roll inside the old bronze boat lamp and pursue the clue of the copper plate engraved with “seven” left by Shen Qingshan and “the eye left behind by the arsonist”—the key to opening the accounts emerges, and the whereabouts of the ledgers and the identity of the mole draw closer. The old object Liu Sanniang guarded for twelve years is finally opened in person, the old bond is renewed, Liu Sanniang obtains some sense of the movements, and Lu Wenfeng also catches hold of the thread.

original.rationale: In this turn, Liu Sanniang has already spoken out the core secret she guarded for twelve years, specific names, the list of informed parties, identifying features, the background of her own lodgers, and the hidden marks on old objects; there is nowhere left to retreat. Shen Qingshan appears in person and hands over key physical evidence and clues. Lu Wenfeng has come carrying the corpse, the boat plaque, and the wax pellet, and has just confirmed outside the abandoned granary that he was transferred away—he was here to reconcile the accounts from the beginning. Both sides have already pushed the talk to the core, the physical evidence is in hand, the setting has been prepared, and the people have gathered; the most likely path is to continue digging deeper along this line.

engagement.user_interest_reading: In this turn, Liu Sanniang gives Lu Wenfeng an answer to his previous question that is more detailed than expected: she not only explains how Qin Zhaoshui 'officially died'—during the autumn flood six years ago, the river-sacrifice boat capsized at Qingwei Shoal; of seven people, only six bodies were recovered; the body was identified by the old helm token at the waist; and he was given a water burial behind the Water God Temple under an unmarked bluestone—but also proactively adds the basis for her judgment that 'I don’t believe it': Old Qin spent his whole life on the water, and the old helm token was never worn at his waist but sewn against the skin into the lining of his left boot. She further gives two possible places he may have gone to ground—the empty grave at the Water God Temple on Qingwei Shoal, and the old shipyard at Xiwan—and one verifiable lead involving a living person: three months ago, someone bought Tendon-Renewing Ointment, old mountain ginseng, and black-snake wine at the South Gate pharmacy, leaving the secret phrase 'Zhaoshui does not shine on lamps.' Finally, she sets the order: 'At daybreak, don’t dig up the granary first; check the grave first; before noon, go to the pharmacy first.' Given Lu Wenfeng’s avoidant, low-extraversion, taciturn but steady personality, what he fears most is asking one question and getting half an answer swallowed, having judgment made on his behalf, and having his words cut off; Liu Sanniang, by contrast, gives him the old case’s inside knowledge all the way to the bottom, preserves the physical evidence as is, and hands the right of judgment back to him ('Don’t take it out yet, don’t compare the prints' is advice rather than an order). In this turn, she again proactively pours out to him all the details behind the Qin Zhaoshui lead. Maintain at the high prior level (0.99).
